一粒金属盐，突然开花: A Grain of Metal Salt Suddenly Blooms
它没有种子，也没有细胞。金属盐粒落进硅酸盐溶液后，彩色矿物管却会一截一截地向上生: It has no seed and no cells. Yet when a grain of metal salt falls into silicate solution, colored mineral tubes grow upward one segment at a time, like underwater coral waking from sleep.
金属离子一碰到硅酸根，就在金属盐粒表面沉淀成一层薄膜。它把浓溶液包在里面，却仍允: When metal ions meet silicate ions, a thin precipitate membrane forms around the grain. It traps the concentrated solution inside, yet still lets water seep through.
水穿过膜，压力在里面上涨: Water Crosses the Membrane. Pressure Rises Within.
膜内的溶液更浓，水会因渗透作用不断进入。体积想变大，薄膜却拦着它——内压于是像一: The solution inside the membrane is more concentrated, so osmosis keeps drawing water in. The volume tries to expand, but the membrane holds it back — internal pressure builds like one slow breath.
膜一破，喷流把管子向上顶: The Membrane Bursts. A Jet Lifts the Tube.
压力超过薄膜能承受的限度，浓溶液从裂口喷出；这里，较轻的内部溶液受浮力偏向上升，: Once the pressure exceeds what the membrane can withstand, concentrated solution jets through a tear. Here, the lighter inner solution tends to rise under buoyancy while precipitation continues where the jet meets the outer solution, leaving a hollow mineral tube behind.
无生命的盐，长成一座花园: Lifeless Salt Grows into a Garden
在一些条件下，膜会重新封住、压力再次积累，让破裂与生长呈现脉冲式重复。海底热液喷: Under some conditions, the membrane reseals and pressure builds again, making rupture and growth repeat in pulses. Precipitation and flow also build mineral chimneys at seafloor hydrothermal vents; that resemblance is a clue, not proof of how life began.
